title: Starting basil from seed
summary: Six to eight weeks before the last frost.
steps: Sow seeds just 3 mm (1/8 in) deep in warm mix.
They sprout in about a week at 21 °C (70 °F) or warmer.
Pinch the top when plants have three pairs of leaves to make them bushy.

title: Picking basil and making pesto
steps: Pinch or cut stems just above a pair of leaves; two new stems grow there.
Pinch off flower buds as soon as you see them.
Blend extra leaves with olive oil and freeze in ice cube trays, adding cheese and nuts when you thaw it.

title: Sowing cilantro
summary: In cool weather, every two to three weeks.
steps: Crush the round seed husks lightly to split them, then sow 1 cm (1/2 in) deep.
Thin to 15 cm (6 in) apart.
In warmer weather, sow in afternoon shade.

title: Picking cilantro and saving coriander
steps: Cut outer stems once plants are 15 cm (6 in) tall.
When plants bolt, let them flower and set seed.
Cut the heads when seeds turn brown and dry them in a paper bag. That's coriander.

title: Sowing dill
summary: Around the last frost, and a few weeks later for pickling time.
steps: Sow 6 mm (1/4 in) deep where it will grow; dill doesn't like being moved.
Thin to 25 cm (10 in).
Plant away from carrots, which can cross with it.

title: Picking dill
summary: Leaves any time, heads for pickles.
steps: Snip feathery leaves as needed.
For pickles, cut flower heads when they open, or when seeds start to form.
Dry leaves on a screen or freeze them chopped.

title: Starting parsley from seed
summary: Eight to ten weeks before the last frost.
steps: Soak seeds overnight in warm water.
Sow 6 mm (1/4 in) deep. Germination takes two to four weeks.
Transplant a couple of weeks before the last frost; parsley handles light frost.

title: Picking parsley
steps: Cut outer stems at the base once the plant has a dozen or so.
Leave the center to keep growing.
Freeze chopped parsley in a little water in ice cube trays.

title: Planting oregano
summary: Around the last frost, in lean, well-drained soil.
steps: Plant small plants 30 cm (12 in) apart in a sunny, dry spot or a pot.
Water until established, then only in long dry spells.
Don't add much compost or fertilizer; rich soil weakens the flavor.

title: Harvesting and drying oregano
steps: Cut stems 10 cm (4 in) long, leaving plenty to regrow.
Tie in small bundles and hang upside down somewhere dark and airy.
When crisp, strip the leaves and store them in a jar.
Cut plants back by half in midsummer to keep them tidy.
